claims.text: Over-abstraction is adding interfaces, layers or general-purpose wrappers for needs nobody has yet; each is more code to read and change, paid for now against a future that may not come; a layer for a future product saves work only if its guessed shape turns out right.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 1; glossary over-abstraction; ADR 0011 lines 37-38 @ stage-4

claims.text: ADR 0011 (status: rejected, Sprint 18) answers a proposal to put every RabbitMQ call behind one broker-neutral interface so that switching broker means writing one new implementation.

IProductRepository has two implementations in DonHang.Catalog, EfProductRepository and ProductCache, the cache wrapping the EF Core repository; CatalogService receives the ProductCache through IProductRepository.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Catalog/EfProductRepository.cs, ProductCache.cs line 13, CatalogModule.cs lines 36-39 (registers ProductCache around EfProductRepository), CatalogService.cs line 7 @ stage-4

claims.text: IOutbox, in DonHang.Domain, declares one method Add(string routingKey, object message); its implementation EfOutbox is in DonHang.Infrastructure; DonHang.Domain references no project.
claims.source_hint: DonHang.Domain/IOutbox.cs; DonHang.Domain/DonHang.Domain.csproj; DonHang.Infrastructure.csproj comment 'only IOutbox lives there' @ stage-4

claims.text: CatalogService.cs lines 5-7: a page of products is a query to shape, so it reads CatalogDbContext directly. Lines 14-28 add the price filter, OrderBy, Skip(offset), Take(limit) to db.Products before it runs and project rows to CatalogProduct.

ADR 0011 lines 42-44 reject the wrapper: no driver today needs another broker, and the layer would hide the features that keep messages from being lost or looping; the ADR records the places to change instead.

ADR 0011 lines 46-57 list nine production files using RabbitMQ.Client (3 in DonHang.Messaging, topology and consumer in Api, Notifications, Payments); lines 59-60 add tests in DonHang.Tests/Messaging/ and /Notifications/.
ADR 0011 lines 20-26: the services rely on RabbitMQ-specific features, among them a dead-letter queue per service (x-dead-letter-exchange) and publisher confirms used by the outbox relay.
ADR 0011 lines 34-38: a neutral interface keeps only what every broker shares, so it either hides dead-letter queue and publisher confirm or exposes them and is no longer neutral.

ADR 0011 lines 68-72 reopen the question when: a requirement needs a feature RabbitMQ lacks; the hosting offers only another broker and the team stops running RabbitMQ; or direct RabbitMQ.Client files grow past estimating from the list.

ADR 0011 lines 76-79: outside the nine files, the outbox, inbox and handler code sees only IOutbox, the JSON message and the service's own calls (never names RabbitMQ), so a switch rewrites those files, not the business rules.

An interface earns its place when it has work today (a second implementation such as a cache, or keeping one project free of another); when the only reason is a possible future switch, go without it and list the switching cost.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 2-5; ADR 0011 Quyết định and Hệ quả @ stage-4

claims.text: Trade-offs: using a class directly adds nothing now; an interface with a present reason is already paid; a neutral layer pays in advance and hides features; using directly with a listed cost keeps the cost known as long as the list stays true.
claims.source_hint: Outline items 2-5; ADR 0011 Các phương án @ stage-4

claims.text: Choices: no repository for the product page while ListAsync has one caller and no cache; a host offering only another broker is a reopen event, recorded in a new ADR sized from the listed files; a new publisher uses DonHang.Messaging.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0011 lines 46-72 @ stage-4; CatalogService.cs @ stage-4; management.l3.superseding-an-adr

claims.text: When every caller lives in the same codebase, adding an interface on the day a second implementation is needed is an ordinary refactoring; an interface added in advance is paid for whether or not the replacement comes.
claims.source_hint: Misconception 1; outline item 1; DonHang.Catalog/IProductRepository.cs line 7 (internal) @ stage-4

claims.text: IOutbox has one production implementation (EfOutbox) and the tests use a fake (DonHang.Tests/FakeOutbox.cs implements IOutbox); its reason is keeping DonHang.Domain free of other projects, not the number of implementations.
At stage-4, git grep -l "using RabbitMQ.Client" stage-4 -- "*.cs" prints 13 files: the nine production files of ADR 0011 plus four under DonHang.Tests/Messaging/ and DonHang.Tests/Notifications/.
